title: Aitaroun: a border town, before and after
summary: Since 1 March 2026: 795 buildings in and around the town seen destroyed on dated satellite pictures, and 5 fires.

steps.title: A border town
text: Aitaroun sits two kilometres from the Blue Line in the district of Bint Jbeil. Green Southerners read the town and the ground within 1.5 km of its houses on sharp satellite pictures, and mapped every change found.
This investigation follows the war of 2026: each change appears on the day it was first seen on a picture, from 1 March 2026.

steps.title: March 2026
text: By the end of March, 5 buildings had been seen destroyed on a dated picture.
steps.note: A change appears on the day it was first seen on a picture, which is when it entered the record, not necessarily when it happened.

steps.title: April 2026
text: By the end of April the count had reached 668: 663 more buildings seen destroyed in one month.

steps.title: What has been mapped since March
text: Since 1 March 2026, 795 buildings in and around the town have been seen destroyed and 50 damaged, and 2.2 km of road cratered or blocked.
Another 2,516 destroyed buildings can be dated only to between two pictures, the first taken before 1 March 2026, so they cannot be placed after 1 March and are not drawn here.

steps.title: Fire round the town
text: 5 fires are recorded at Aitaroun, from 2 July 2026 to 15 August 2026: 2 linked to an Israeli attack and lit by an explosion, and 3 in the yellow-line zone with no attack linked to them. Where a burn scar was measured, 4 of them cover 114.0 ha between them.

steps.title: The other records
text: The corpus also holds 10 detonations and demolitions, 2 displacement orders and 2 white phosphorus attacks for Aitaroun, each counted apart.

steps.title: Read it yourself
text: Open the database on Aitaroun to read the town's figures by kind, date and column, and play the timeline over its mapped damage from 1 March 2026. The records themselves are not published; to access them, contact Green Southerners.
